turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Good morning, sir. Please come in and sit, I will check the pressure and the pulse before doctor calls you.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Good morning, sister. Thank you. I hope we have not kept the clinic waiting.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Not at all. Blood pressure is one thirty eight over eighty six, pulse is seventy four. You can go through.
[SEG0004] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He was saying the parking is too tight today, that is why we hurried.
[SEG0005] person_4 (DOCTOR): Good morning. I am Dr. Menon. Please tell me, what brings you today?
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): Good morning, doctor. I am having pain on the outer side of my right elbow. It is troubling my work.
[SEG0007] person_4 (DOCTOR): The outer side. Umm, how long would you say?
[SEG0008] person_2 (PATIENT): Err, it is six weeks now, doctor. It came slowly, not from one fall or one knock.
[SEG0009] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): He is a carpenter, doctor, furniture and door frames. He will not sit even on Sunday.
[SEG0010] person_4 (DOCTOR): I see. And when does this pain become worse?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): When I lift a cup of tea, doctor, even that. Also when I grip the chisel or the hammer for some time.
[SEG0012] person_4 (DOCTOR): Any swelling at the elbow? Any numbness or tingling in the fingers?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. No swelling. And no numbness, no tingling. The hand is working.
[SEG0014] person_4 (DOCTOR): Does the pain start from the neck or shoot down from the shoulder?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. It stays at the elbow itself. The neck is fine.
[SEG0016] person_4 (DOCTOR): Alright, let me feel. I am pressing the outer bony point of the right elbow. Is this the place?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor, that is the exact place. Kindly, a little gentler.
[SEG0018] person_4 (DOCTOR): Sorry. Now cock the wrist up against my hand. Yes, that brings the pain. I do not see redness, and I do not see swelling.
[SEG0019] person_1 (NURSE): I will shift this stool. My sister takes biotin for her hair, she never stops talking about those tablets, but that is her business, not yours, sir.

[SEG0020] person_4 (DOCTOR): So, let me think aloud. The forearm muscles attach on that outer point, and repeated gripping irritates the tendon there. This is what we call tennis elbow, even though, umm, you are not playing tennis.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor, only carpentry, since many years. I have two helpers in the workshop, but I still do the fine fitting myself.
[SEG0022] person_4 (DOCTOR): What all medicines are you taking? For the elbow or for anything else.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): Amlodipine five milligrams in the morning, for the pressure. And the cholesterol one at night.
[SEG0024] person_4 (DOCTOR): The cholesterol one. Do you recall the name?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): I am sorry, doctor, the name is not coming. It is ten milligrams at night, a small white tablet. That is all I remember.
[SEG0026] person_2 (PATIENT): Also the sugar tablets, five hundred milligrams, morning and evening. Umm, the proper name escapes me just now.
[SEG0027] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I was supposed to bring the strips. I left them near the gas stove, completely my fault.
[SEG0028] person_2 (PATIENT): For the elbow I take ibuprofin. Four hundred, uh, four hundred milligrams, twice a day, after food, since about ten days.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning, one teaspoon. It is aswagandha, from the shop near our house. Nothing else.
[SEG0030] person_4 (DOCTOR): Noted. Please bring those strips next time, I should not guess the names. I will leave the pressure tablet as it is.
[SEG0031] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): Doctor, my brother takes metformin, the five hundred milligram one, for his own sugar. I wondered if it is the same, but I must not assume.
[SEG0032] person_4 (DOCTOR): Quite right, do not assume. Your brother's tablet is not your husband's tablet.
[SEG0033] person_1 (NURSE): These houses, I tell you. My little boy had fever last month and the medicine box was upside down for days. We will sort the names next time.
[SEG0034] person_4 (DOCTOR): For the elbow, please continue the ibuprofen four hundred milligrams twice a day, and always after food. Not on an empty stomach.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Yes, doctor. It brings the pain down a little, I must say. Not fully.
[SEG0036] person_4 (DOCTOR): I am not injecting today. If it has not settled with a brace and physiotherapy, we might consider a steroid injection later. Not as a first step.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): I would prefer to avoid the injection, doctor, if you think that is reasonable.
[SEG0038] person_4 (DOCTOR): It is reasonable. Please buy a tennis elbow brace, the strap just below the sore point, and wear it while you work. I will refer you for physiotherapy.
[SEG0039] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): There is one physio by the temple. Or will your side arrange it?

[SEG0040] person_4 (DOCTOR): Our reception will book the physiotherapy, so kindly wait at the desk. Also, no heavy timber with the right arm for a few weeks, and ice the outer elbow ten minutes after work.
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): I will do that, doctor. The helpers can lift. I will only mark and supervise.
[SEG0042] person_4 (DOCTOR): If I ask you to score the pain, ten being the worst, where is it?
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Six, doctor. Sometimes seven, mostly when I lift the cup in the morning.
[SEG0044] person_4 (DOCTOR): Does it wake you at night?
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): No, doctor. Sleep is alright. I am able to sleep.

[SEG0046] person_4 (DOCTOR): Right. My working impression is lateral epicondylitis, tennis elbow, right side. The story and the examination fit. I am not thinking of an infection in the joint, or a pinched nerve.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): That is reassuring, doctor. If it worsens before the physio, what should I do?
[SEG0048] person_4 (DOCTOR): If the pain becomes severe, or the elbow swells up, or you get fever, come back sooner. Otherwise I will see you in four weeks.
[SEG0049] person_3 (FAMILY_MEMBER): I will bring him, doctor. He will try to say the orders are pending.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): I will come, doctor. Thank you for explaining it properly. I am grateful.
[SEG0051] person_4 (DOCTOR): You are welcome. Take care of that arm.
[SEG0052] person_1 (NURSE): Sir, I will print the physio slip. Please wait two minutes at the desk, the printer is slow today.

spec.situation: Painter or carpenter with outer elbow pain for six weeks, worse lifting a cup; takes ibuprofen; physio and brace advice; no injection yet.

traps.happens: The patient lists medicines with their purpose ('amlodipine for the pressure', 'the cholesterol one at night', 'sugar tablets') and also mentions a herbal or shop remedy in passing ('only the Ayurvedic powder in the morning'). Their chronic conditions are never asked about directly.
traps.label_rule: Each medicine is recorded with the dose and timing said for THAT medicine; the herbal remedy is a medicine too (currently_used). A condition the patient states through its medicine ('for the pressure') is a past_medical_history entry ONLY if the patient actually said the condition name or its everyday name ('the pressure' = hypertension, normalized); do not invent a duration.

traps.happens: The doctor (or nurse) explains a mechanism or a diagnosis in the patient's body ('the voice box is irritated by reflux', 'diabetes dulls the nerves in the feet', 'the swelling is your body fighting infection'). A nurse or caregiver also mentions a fact about THEIR OWN life (their sister, their child, their own illness).
traps.label_rule: Explanations by the doctor are NEVER symptoms, history or social history of the patient; they may only appear as clinical_assessment or counselling if the doctor stated them as such. A nurse's or caregiver's own life facts are not recorded as the patient's. Each symptom's reported_by is the person who really described it.

features: third_party_medicine: someone mentions a medicine or condition that belongs to a relative or friend (the sister's biotin, the husband's metformin). It must not appear as the patient's own; a relative's illness can only be family history if said as such.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

omissions.text: Past medical history of diabetes mellitus is implied by the patient's ongoing 'sugar tablets' taken 500 mg morning and evening, but no diabetes history is recorded.
Doctor stated he would leave the blood pressure tablet unchanged.
Doctor explicitly said he was not injecting today.
Doctor stated he was not thinking of an infection in the joint or a pinched nerve.

Physiotherapy booking plan was specific: reception would book it and the patient should wait at the desk; nurse also said she would print the physio slip and asked him to wait two minutes at the desk.
Patient expressed a preference to avoid steroid injection if reasonable, and doctor agreed this was reasonable.
